A key pressed again quickly is its next letter (twice, the second), and nothing else; once, the input method still guesses which; off, every press is a key

Predictive: each key is any of its letters and the word is guessed (4663 for good, home, gone); multi-tap: a key pressed again quickly is its next letter. Address fields and fields that ask for no suggestions are always multi-tap
How long the pen stays up before what is written counts as one character and the next begins: shorter for a fast hand, longer if you pause between strokes
Which letters each key types: up to five, a letter may be on more than one key
Tap a key to set the letters it types, up to five. A letter may be on more than one key; pinyin with a letter on no key cannot be typed.
Letters a to z, each once, in the order the key shows them and multi-tap goes through them
Put every key back to its letters as on a phone?
What a long press on a key offers besides its digit and letters

Tap a key to set the symbols its long press offers too, above its digit and letters, a line between. With Chinese punctuation on, those of 2 to 9 type as Chinese punctuation (! types ！); those of 1 type as they are.
Apart by spaces, up to %1$d. A digit or a letter alone is not kept: a long press types those as keys, not as themselves. Emptied, the key offers none.
Put every key back to its default symbols?
None of those can be a symbol (a digit or a letter alone): the key is left as it was.
Higher picks better and uses more battery
Low: by how common words and pairs are, least battery
Medium: weighs the whole sentence at every key
High: a larger model picks the first again as you pause, most accurate

Outlined keys are ones you changed. A faded key offers nothing when held, and types nothing when swiped.
While typing Chinese, the key on the left types the punctuation on the right; a key with several offers a choice. Tap one to change or remove it.
